title: Regulations & Funding
before:
Career and technical education (CTE) is governed by State and federal regulations. The federal compliance office is the Office of Vocational and Adult Education. The State Board of Education is the state governing board. 

Bond Funding
  • Career and Technical Education Equipment Bond  
  • RFA Selection Packet
  • Request for Equipment Change (Awardee Request Form)

  • Receipt Tracker for invoice submission

  • For additional information reach out to Ernest Kumah at Ernest.Kumah@maine.gov  
State Funding
  • CTE EPS Funds (formula) 
  • Grants4ME
  • CTE Program Update Funds (formula)
  • CTE Early Childhood Funds (distribution yet to be determined)
  • Education CTE Supply Funds (formula - FY2023 only)
Federal Funding
  • Perkins Funds (formula)
  • Grants4ME
  • ARP Equipment and Personnel Infrastructure Funds (RFA)
  • ARP Infrastructure Funds (RFA)
Regulations
  • State: 
    - Chapter 313 of Title 20-A  
    - Program Approval, Chapter 231
    - Standard Criteria, Chapter 232
    - Program Evaluation, Chapter 236
    - Live/Outside Work, Chapter 237 
    - Regional School Calendars 
    - Equal Educational Opportunity, Chapter 4
  • Federal: All CTE schools are subject to the federal Carl D. Perkins Act and the Education Department General Administrative Regulations.  
Methods of Administration (MOA)

The Department conducts CTE site visits as part of its Vocational Education MOA civil rights compliance of districts that receive federal funding.

  • MOA Resources

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 1 list item opens with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Let a colon do its own work
decisions.why: A colon marks the words before it as a term and the words after it as what the term means. Here 1 list item opens with a term set in the same weight as its own explanation, so the list cannot be scanned. 1 link sits immediately in front of a colon, where the chevron lands between the term and the punctuation that belongs to it. No word changes and nothing is removed.

decisions.label: Make a loose address look like an address
decisions.why: 1 email address sits in the body of this page rather than in a contact block, drawn exactly like every other link — so the one that opens a mail window looks the same as the ones that go to web pages. The chip carries the same envelope the banner's contact link uses. The address itself does not change.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
